newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth agrees to reduce access charges.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth agrees to reduce access charges.

text.p: BellSouth Corp Friday said it agreed to reduce access charges paid by long distance companies for access to its local network by approximately $38 million.
The agreement settles a dispute with MCI Communications Corp and Sprint Corp which arose out of 1995 legislation that opened Tennessee's local telecommunications market to competition.

BellSouth officials said they will file requests with the Tennessee Regulatory Authority as early as Friday to reduce access charges by approximately $9 million effective February 15, and an additional $8 million effective July 1, 1997. The remaining reductions will become effective either January 1, 1998, or when BellSouth's price regulation plan goes into effect, whichever is later.

It said the reductions, which apply to all long distance companies, will cause Tennessee's intrastate access charges to mirror interstate access charges that were in effect on August 1, 1995. Interstate access charges fall under the jurisdiction of the U.S. Federal Communications Commission.

"This reduction to the long distance companies should be a tremendous boon for Tennessee consumers in the form of lower long distance prices for calls handled by all the long distance companies within Tennessee," said DeWitt Ezell, BellSouth's Tennessee president.

"It will create a significant savings for consumers if the long distance companies pass on this reduction dollar- for-dollar to consumers. We're glad that we could reach this agreement to promote competition and lower prices in Tennessee and to avoid further legal action," he added.
